abstract.t: This document is the PIC Revocation Specification, a subordinate specification of the PIC Specification. It defines how authority is revoked within the Provenance Identity Continuity (PIC) Model.

Expiry bounds how long a continuity state may be accepted; revocation withdraws validity before that bound. PIC revocation preserves the core model invariants: exactly one predecessor per non-root advancement, Proof of Relationship, authority non-expansion, and no authority import from unrelated continuities.

For a linear revocation profile, a stable authenticated lineage/PCA identifier plus a continuity position can name a causal suffix. In a fan-out profile, the same pair names a lineage and path depth but does not uniquely name an occurrence or its causal descendants: sibling states may share the same position. Branch-selective or occurrence-selective revocation therefore requires an additional authenticated occurrence, checkpoint, branch, or ancestry coordinate. This document calls the stable lineage identifier PCA ID. Additional authenticated selectors, such as grant, issuer, key, delegate, attestation, or policy selectors, may be used by a profile but do not replace the required causal coordinates when descendants, rather than a whole lineage-depth range, must be invalidated.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: This section is non-normative. It introduces the revocation model used by this document.

PIC continuity starts from a trusted root PIC Context of Authority, or PCA, and advances through non-root continuity advancements. A revocation that must affect an entire lineage or depth range needs a stable way to name the root authority context and the path position at which validity stops. A revocation that must affect only descendants of one occurrence in a fan-out graph additionally needs authenticated occurrence identity and ancestry.

In PIC Profile 0.2, a trusted settlement authority issues settled PIC Token JWTs carrying settled PIC Continuity COSE artifacts. A workload may propose exactly one advancement in a workload-signed candidate PIC Token JWT whose candidate PIC Continuity COSE carries exactly one PIC Continuity Transition COSE. The settlement authority validates that candidate and, if it accepts the advancement, issues the next settled PIC Token JWT. Settled Profile 0.2 Continuity COSE artifacts have transitions = null and do not carry a replayable transition history.

Revocation state remains external and dynamic. Revoking a PCA, position, key, delegate, attestation, grant, issuer, or policy does not rewrite signed PIC PCA COSE checkpoints and does not rebuild historical transitions. Verifiers and settlement services evaluate authenticated revocation state against the presented continuity state.

The current PIC-X 0.2.3 binding requires a signed PCA lineage_id, preserves it across advancement, and mirrors it into PIC Token JWT jti; it also preserves a signed PCA position. These are useful authenticated revocation coordinates. PIC-X 0.2.3 nevertheless configures the PIC revocation hook as a no-op and implements no PIC revocation state. Absolute expires_at and settlement-key retention bound acceptance but are not early revocation [4].

section.name: Requirements Notation
section.t: The normative sections of this document are Sections 2, 3, 4, and 5. Sections 1 and 6 are non-normative.

The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [2] [3] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals within normative text.

section.name: Revocation Coordinates
section.t: This section is normative.

section.name: PCA ID
section.t: A revocation profile that supports causal lineage or suffix revocation MUST define a stable authenticated PCA ID or equivalent lineage/PCA identifier. The PCA ID identifies the trusted continuity origin and revocation domain. It is stable across successor checkpoints; a changing checkpoint hash identifies one occurrence and is not the lineage identifier unless a profile explicitly defines a separate checkpoint-scoped revocation domain.

The PCA ID MUST be bound to the relevant trusted PCA checkpoint artifact or to authenticated metadata covered by the selected revocation profile. It MUST NOT be a freely chosen unauthenticated value. The selected revocation profile MUST define its representation, authentication, issuer or authority, lookup and validation procedure, freshness, rollback protection, and unavailable-state behavior.

This document does not define one universal wire claim or field carrying the PCA ID. It also does not define JWT jti as the PCA ID for every profile. A profile MAY map a concrete claim, field, artifact hash, or authenticated metadata item to the PCA ID only when that mapping is explicitly defined and authenticated by that profile.
Current Profile 0.2 settled PIC Continuity COSE carries the exact signed current PIC PCA COSE checkpoint bytes at:
The corresponding signed-artifact hash is carried at:

Those fields identify the current trusted checkpoint artifact for Profile 0.2 validation. In the current PIC-X binding, the signed PCA lineage_id is the stable lineage/PCA identifier and the PIC Token JWT jti MUST equal it. The base Profile 0.2 artifact schema leaves lineage_id optional, while PIC-X requires it. root.pca_hash identifies one checkpoint and MUST NOT be substituted for the stable lineage_id when the intended revocation scope is the whole lineage.

section.name: Position
section.t: A revocation profile that supports causal suffix revocation MUST expose or authenticate a continuity position.

The position identifies causal order along one path within the continuity rooted at the PCA ID. The root position and the progression from each predecessor to each successor MUST be unambiguous. A non-root advancement MUST have the position required by the selected continuity profile.

Position is not a global event identifier. In a fan-out profile, two incomparable sibling states MAY have the same PCA ID and position. A profile MUST NOT infer that equal positions identify one occurrence, or that numeric ordering alone proves ancestry across branches.

The profile MUST reject missing, negative, fractional, non-canonical, overflowing, wrapping, or otherwise invalid positions. A profile MUST NOT introduce a second mandatory counter solely for revocation when the continuity profile already defines positions.
For current Profile 0.2, position is carried by PIC PCA COSE checkpoints and PIC Continuity Transition COSE artifacts. PIC Continuity COSE itself does not carry a position field.

section.t: For a profile that guarantees one accepted state at each position, the linear causal coordinate for suffix revocation is:
A causal suffix cutoff is:
It matches a presented continuity state when:

In a profile that permits fan-out, this predicate defines a lineage-depth cutoff: it applies across every branch sharing the PCA ID at or beyond the selected depth. It does not mean “descendants of one selected occurrence.” A profile that claims occurrence-selective or branch-selective causal revocation MUST additionally authenticate an occurrence or checkpoint identifier and the ancestry relation by which the presented state descends from it.
Whole-continuity revocation is the root-position case and is unaffected by fan-out. The selected profile MUST define the root position used for that comparison.
Knowledge of the PCA ID, the position, or both MUST NOT authorize revocation. Targeting and revocation authorization are separate.

section.name: Revocation Semantics
section.t: This section is normative where BCP 14 language is used.

section.name: Attenuation Is Not Revocation
section.t: Attenuation of a selected continuity advancement changes only the materialized authority of the accepted successor lineage. It MUST NOT be interpreted as revocation of the predecessor checkpoint, invalidation of that predecessor, or invalidation of another otherwise-valid sibling continuation from the same predecessor. Invalidating those states requires authenticated revocation state under the selected revocation profile.

section.t: In a linear profile, a suffix cutoff invalidates the selected position and its causal future:

In a fan-out profile, the same comparison invalidates all matching branches at the selected position or greater and is therefore a lineage-depth cutoff, not a branch-selective causal suffix. The profile MUST name that broader scope explicitly. If only descendants of one occurrence are to be invalidated, the profile MUST use the additional occurrence/ancestry coordinate required by Section 2.3.
The exact wire representation and any concrete revocation-profile naming for these operations are profile-defined.

section.name: Optional Selectors
section.t: A revocation profile MAY define additional authenticated selectors, including:

list.t: grant binding;
origin issuer;
key or verification method;
executor or delegate;
attestation;
policy;
resource, tenant, or security-domain selector;
another explicitly profile-defined authenticated selector.

section.t: These selectors are administrative or evidentiary criteria. They do not replace the causal coordinates required by the selected scope. In a linear profile those coordinates may be (PCA ID, position); in a branch-selective profile they additionally identify the selected occurrence and authenticate ancestry.

Possession or knowledge of a selector value MUST NOT authorize revocation. For example, knowledge of a grant identifier, PCA ID, key identifier, issuer identifier, or position is not a revocation credential.

section.name: Historical Selector Resolution
section.t: When a selector refers to historical evidence that is not present in every descendant continuity state, a profile that wants causal retroactive effect MUST resolve that selector to an authenticated affected position:

figure.sourcecode: KEY / DELEGATE / ATTESTATION / ISSUER / other selector | v authenticated affected position | v (PCA ID, fromPosition)

section.t: The resolver MUST authenticate the selector occurrence, the PCA ID, the position, the integrity of the evidence used for resolution, and the authority to materialize the resulting cutoff.

When fan-out is possible, resolving only to (PCA ID, fromPosition) intentionally creates a lineage-depth cutoff across sibling branches. A resolver that intends branch-selective effect MUST also authenticate the selected occurrence and descendant relation. It MUST NOT infer ancestry from numeric position alone.

A bare assertion that a selector occurred at a position MUST NOT be sufficient. A valid position witness MAY be an authenticated settled continuity artifact, an authenticated transition extract, an authenticated historical-index record, a checkpoint, a Merkle inclusion proof, a succinct proof, or another profile-defined authenticated witness.

For a compromised-key revocation, a position witness authenticated only by the compromised key MUST NOT be sufficient evidence that the position was accepted into the continuity. The revocation authority MUST require corroboration independent of the revoked key, such as an authenticated index, a trusted validator record, a checkpoint, or another profile-defined proof.

section.name: Dynamic Restrictions
section.t: A profile MAY define dynamic authority or execution-contract restrictions. Such restrictions are evaluated as external authenticated state against the presented PCA ID, position, and optional selectors.

Dynamic restrictions MUST be monotonic: they may only make effective authority or execution conformance equally or more restrictive. They MUST NOT rewrite signed PCA checkpoint artifacts, mutate historical transitions, alter predecessor uniqueness, replace Proof of Relationship, or expand authority.

This monotonic external state is compatible with treating revocation as an additional ordered security-state coordinate: ordinary state updates may only restrict acceptance. Any relaxation is a separate re-origination or explicitly authorized relaxation event, not an ordinary continuation [5].
The profile MUST define restriction scope, composition, conflict resolution, freshness, rollback protection, and unavailable-state behavior.

section.name: Revocation Authorization
section.t: This section is normative.

Every accepted revocation or dynamic restriction MUST be authenticated by an authorized revocation authority. A matching target coordinate is necessary for targeting but never sufficient for authorization.
A profile MUST define how each revocation authority is proven. Possible authorities include:

texttable.c: the PCA ID it is authorized to administer
profile-defined issuer authorization and revocation proof
authenticated grant binding and grant-authority proof
continuities whose profile authenticates that issuer binding
its own future, as permitted by policy
authenticated position proof and policy authority
uses of a key, delegate, attestation, or issuer selector
selector proof plus authority to materialize a causal cutoff

section.t: An executor at position k MUST NOT revoke a position upstream of itself unless it separately holds root, grant, issuer, or other profile-defined revocation authority. A policy MAY allow an executor to revoke its own future from k+1, or from k when the current position itself must be invalidated.

Grant revocation MUST be accepted only when the Verifier can establish that the revocation issuer is authorized for the grant. Possession or knowledge of a grant identifier alone MUST NOT authorize revocation.

section.name: Revocation State
section.t: This section is normative.
Revocation state is external, authenticated, and append-only. A profile MUST specify:

list.t: how revocation state is authenticated;
how freshness is determined;
how rollback is detected;
who defines the minimum acceptable revocation-state version;
how that minimum is authenticated;
what happens when required revocation state is unavailable.

section.t: Unavailable-state behavior MUST be explicit. Examples include fail closed, accept only a fresh stapled proof, accept within a bounded offline window, or another profile-defined behavior.
Security revocations and restrictions applied to a PCA ID, position, grant, selector, or policy scope MUST be append-only and MUST become only equally or more restrictive over time:

figure.sourcecode: effectiveRevocationState(t + 1) is at least as restrictive as effectiveRevocationState(t)

section.t: A relaxation MUST require a new grant, a new trusted root authority context, a new PCA ID, or another profile-defined re-origination mechanism. It MUST NOT be implemented by deleting an existing revocation, replaying an older revocation view, replacing active state with less restrictive state, or silently un-revoking an existing cutoff.

section.name: Future Branch-Capable Profiles
section.t: This section is non-normative.

PIC can support branch-capable revocation in a future or separate profile, but branch-domain machinery is not part of the current centralized Profile 0.2 base coordinate. PIC-X currently permits sibling fan-out from one checkpoint; its lineage_id plus position therefore supports whole-lineage and lineage-depth targeting, not unique branch or occurrence targeting. This document does not define branch-domain fields, branch-suffix strategies, branch-creation evidence, parent branch ancestry, or branch-domain escape rules for Profile 0.2.

A future branch-capable profile would need to define bounded authenticated branch coordinates, branch-creation authorization, anti-escape validation order, branch-selective cutoff authorization, historical resolution rules, and privacy properties. Those details are intentionally out of scope for this revision.

section.name: Position Capacity
section.t: This appendix is non-normative. If a profile represents continuity position with a finite integer domain, exhausting that domain requires completing that many causal advancements on one path:

figure.sourcecode: secondsToOverflow = (2^64 - 1 - currentPosition) / R where R = maximum accepted advancements per second on one continuity path

section.t: Each path is causally sequential; fan-out permits several paths but does not parallelize one path. A concrete R depends on hardware, network, and application logic and is not fixed here. Under any realistic per-path rate a uint64 position is practically inexhaustible, though a profile that wants the mathematically unbounded case may use an unbounded integer encoding. The normative point is only that overflow and wraparound are rejected when the selected representation can overflow.

section.name: Origins, Authorship, and Historical Record
section.t: This section is informative and is included so that the document preserves its provenance when distributed independently.

The Provenance Identity Continuity (PIC) Model was originally developed by Nicola Gallo as a formal framework for reasoning about causal authority propagation across distributed execution. Its development introduced Proof of Relationship (PoR), Proof of Continuity (PoC), authority non-expansion, relational attenuation, and event-level causal provenance as connected parts of the framework. The PIC Specifications translate those formal results into technical requirements and are published and maintained by Nitro Agility S.r.l. as Specification Steward.

section.name: Implementation Status
section.t: This section is informative and records implementation coverage at the time of this draft.

PIC-X 0.2.3 authenticates stable lineage_id and position coordinates that can support future revocation profiles, but its current revocation hook is a no-op and it implements no PIC revocation state. Expiration and settlement-key retention are lifetime controls, not the early revocation mechanism specified here.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: Revocation security depends on authenticated, fresh, rollback-protected revocation state and explicit behavior when that state is unavailable. Stale or rolled-back state can cause a Verifier or settlement service to accept continuity that should have been cut off. A selector value, PCA ID, position, key identifier, grant identifier, or policy label is only a target coordinate; knowledge or possession of it is not revocation authority.

In a fan-out profile, (PCA ID, position) is not a unique causal-event coordinate. Treating it as one can either over-revoke independent siblings or falsely claim branch-selective semantics. A branch-selective profile needs authenticated occurrence identity and ancestry.

Selector-to-position resolution needs authenticated evidence that the selector occurred at the affected continuity position. For compromised key revocation, evidence authenticated only by the compromised key is not sufficient where this document requires independent corroboration. Dynamic restrictions need to remain monotonic: they can make effective authority or execution-contract conformance more restrictive, but cannot rewrite signed checkpoints, mutate history, replace Proof of Relationship, or expand authority.

section.name: Privacy Considerations
section.t: Revocation lookups and distribution can expose stable lineage identifiers, positions, issuers, keys, delegates, resources, and policy selectors. Branch or occurrence coordinates can reveal execution structure. Profiles should disclose only the selectors needed for the selected scope, prevent unauthorized enumeration, and define retention, access-control, and correlation boundaries for revocation records.

section.name: Registry Considerations
section.t: This document defines abstract revocation operations and requests no external registry action. Concrete wire profiles may define registries for revocation operations, selector types, status values, and error codes.
